prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Predictions were generally too high compared to noise-corrected outcomes across most tests.
For finish, new_flow (2 tests), no statistically significant win was achieved and no clear effect was seen, despite positive noise-corrected averages (+2.2%).
Evidence is still too thin to establish rules for adoption (new_flow, redesign), finish (new_screen), and sign_in (reorder), as each has only one test.
No kind of change has been proven helpful yet, as no test has yielded a statistically significant win.

Measured so far, by kind of change (relative change on the target step):
- adoption, new_flow: -2.3% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- adoption, redesign: -1.4% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- finish, new_flow: +2.2% after noise correction, 2 test(s)
- finish, new_screen: -4.0% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- sign_in, reorder: -6.3% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)

Funnel:
- choose_path: 76.2%, median 8s / mean 514s
- sign_in: 72.9%, median 3s / mean 567s
- adoption: 60.9%, median 89s / mean 1017s
- home: 81.3%, median 201s / mean 2336s
- finish: 64.8%, median 395s / mean 5815s
- finishing onboarding overall: 17.8%

Return JSON {"scores": [{"index": i, "impact": n, "evidence": n, "confidence": n, "cost": n,
"predicted_lift": x, "note": short}]}

Changes:
0: [sign_in, layout] Sign In Layout Split View: Re-layouts the sign-in screen into a side-by-side split view highlighting account safety and cloud pet backups. (why: Sign-in drops 27.1% of users, and 8 support tickets noted pets going missing or resetting upon re-logging.)
1: [adoption, redesign] Photo Upload Stage Redesign: Redesigns the photo upload screen into a stage view with clear upload area replace components. (why: Adoption conversion drops to 60.9% and 3 support emails reported custom pet generation failures or distorted output.)
2: [choose_path, new_screen] Onboarding Path Overview Screen: Inserts an explicit path overview screen right before choosing a path to clarify adoption options. (why: Path selection drops 23.8% of users with high mean time (514s), indicating hesitation and lack of upfront clarity.)
3: [home, wait_info] Waiting Generation Progress Time Estimate: Enables animated progress, explicit time estimates, and helpful tips on the waiting screen during pet rendering. (why: Users spend a median 201s (mean 2336s) on the waiting step with a 18.7% dropoff rate and reports of stalled apps.)
4: [sign_in, hint] Existing Account Pet Sync Hint: Adds a prominent notice explaining how signing into an existing account restores existing pet profiles. (why: 8 support tickets (largest theme) reported pets missing or resetting after signing back into an account.)
5: [finish, new_flow] Desktop Setup Readiness Sub Flow: Adds a sub-flow before finishing to ensure the desktop overlay permissions are ready before launching. (why: 3 support tickets reported pet failing to show on desktop or app refusing to open after setup.)
6: [choose_path, copy] Clear Path Choice Headline Clarification: Updates headline and body to clearly differentiate standard pet adoption versus custom photo pet creation. (why: choose_path drops 23.8% of users and has an abnormally high mean completion time of 514s.)
7: [home, notification] Background Generation Ready Alert: Adds an opt-in system notification toggle so users can minimize the app while pet generation completes. (why: The waiting step has extremely long mean times (2336s), causing users to close or abandon the app.)

scores.note: Sign-in dropoff and ticket volume are high, but major layout structural changes carry moderate execution risk.
Adoption has massive dropoff, but previous adoption redesign test resulted in a -1.4% drop.
Adding a new screen to choose_path adds friction; new_screen test history shows -4.0% relative loss.
Extremely long wait times lead to stalled app perception; explicit progress time estimate reduces perceived waiting friction.
Addresses the top support complaint (8 tickets) with a low-cost, zero-friction copy hint.
Finish step has high dropoff and tickets, but adding a sub-flow adds step friction (+2.2% finish new_flow historical mean was non-significant).
High mean time on choose_path suggests confusion; headline copy clarification is low-cost and safe.
Directly targets high mean time (2336s) on background generation, though OS notification prompt adds slight complexity.
